Now we have copper_test solution (15 mL) containing dissolved Cu (sky-blue). We can filter to remove any precipitate (none). But we can use copper_test as solution containing Cu and possibly Co? The Co may have dissolved as well, giving light cyan earlier. After adding NH3, solution turned pale sky-blue, indicating Cu complex dominates. Co may also be present but color may be masked.

We need to isolate alkali cations. The test_K2CrO4 solution still contains alkali cations (Na, K, etc.) plus maybe some leftover Cu/Co if not fully precipitated. But we added K2CrO4 to filtrate after removing precipitate; no precipitate formed, so Cu and Co remained in solution. So test_K2CrO4 still contains Cu2+ (blue) and Co2+ (pink) plus alkali. The flame test gave multi-colored.

We could try to precipitate Cu and Co using H2S acidic to remove them, leaving alkali. Let's use test_K2CrO4 as sol1. Use H2S(acidic).
